title: Tenancy agreements: written information for your tenant
text:
From 1 May 2026, you will need to give tenants certain written information about key terms of the tenancy.

There is certain information that you must provide. If you do not, your tenant could complain to the local council, and you could receive a fine of up to £7,000.

You will need to give this information when you create a new tenancy on or after 1 May 2026. You will need to do this before you sign a tenancy agreement or otherwise agree the tenancy.

You may include this information in a written tenancy agreement, but you can give it separately.

See the list of information that you will need to include, which was published on 20 March 2026:

## Written information that must be given to tenants - landlord guidance

PDF, 219 KB, 10 pages

A first draft version of this was published on 24 February 2026. Some small changes have been made to this final published version, so you may wish to check again if you looked at this before 20 March 2026.

You can also see the Statutory Instrument that puts this into law. A Statutory Instrument is created by the government and they are the most common form of secondary legislation.

Statutory Instrument written information for your tenant

## If you already rent out a property to tenants

You will not need to provide this information to an existing tenant if:

- the tenancy agreement was signed before 1 May 2026
- you have a written record of the agreement between you and your tenant – for example, you have a written tenancy agreement

Instead, you need to give your tenants a government produced document, called ‘The Renters’ Rights Act Information Sheet 2026’. This will explain to your tenants how their tenancy might be affected by the changes to the law.

This has been published online. You have until 31 May to give it to your tenants. You must give it to all tenants named on a tenancy agreement. You can give it by either:

- printing a hard copy, which is posted or given to the tenants by hand.
- sending the PDF electronically as an attachment, for example, to an email or text message.

If the tenancy is based entirely on a verbal agreement and you made this agreement before 1 May 2026, then you cannot give the Information Sheet. You must provide the written information about key terms of the tenancy instead. You must give this to your tenants by 31 May 2026.
